findings.text: follow-on: `server_for_registration` resolves through `_server_index`, whose keys are the declaration's own spellings matched exactly (`imas_ambix/agent/registry.py:62` builds `server.name`, `server.host`, `_short_host(server.host)` with no case folding), while the CLI comparison this commit removes lowercased BOTH sides (`record.host.split('.', 1)[0].lower()` against `server.host.split('.', 1)[0].lower()`, visible at 388f66ff:imas_ambix/agent/cli.py), so a registration whose host differs from the declaration in case now resolves to no declared server instead of to its server. The consequence is the failure this commit exists to prevent -- the serve reads as unplaced and a restart or key rotation moves it onto the site's first server, onto a partition, account and reservation its job was never admitted under. It is a narrowing on an unreachable-in-practice spelling rather than a live defect, because the registration host is written by the launch as `$(hostname)` (imas_ambix/agent/slurm.py:936 and :955 emit it) and declared hosts are written by hand, so no case mismatch is produced on this site and no test covers one; recorded rather than repaired, since the node is otherwise complete and the check would belong with the index rather than with either caller.

follow-on: `server_for_registration` rebuilds the index on every call (`_server_index(servers)` inside the function body, `imas_ambix/agent/registry.py:98`), and `build_endpoint_document` calls it once per registration at `imas_ambix/agent/registry.py:504`, so the document build now costs servers x registrations where the builder previously hoisted the index once out of the loop (388f66ff:imas_ambix/agent/registry.py `index = _server_index(servers)` above the registration loop). Harmless at this site's scale -- a handful of servers and a handful of registrations -- and the function is public so it cannot hoist its own, but a caller building a large document pays it repeatedly.
